name: Weeping Cave
summary: Toxic blight seeps through Weeping Cave in the northeastern hills of the Western Plaguelands, just west of the Thondroril River. Grotesque fungal beasts and oozes shelter in its tunnels.

sections.title: A Den of Rot
sections.body: Above the Thondroril River, moisture trickles through Weeping Cave’s rocky ceiling. The Scourge’s plague has poisoned the soil overhead, and foul runoff drains into the dark tunnels. Rotting horrors and decaying behemoths roam there with caustic oozes. A corrupted elemental called The Husk dwells in the cave as well.

faq.q: Where is the Weeping Cave located?
faq.answer: Weeping Cave lies in the northeastern hills of the Western Plaguelands, just west of the Thondroril River near the Eastern Plaguelands border.

faq.q: What creatures dwell inside the cave?
faq.answer: Rotting behemoths, decaying horrors, toxic creeping slimes, and a rare elemental called The Husk dwell inside Weeping Cave.

faq.q: Why is it called the Weeping Cave?
aliases: why is it called weeping cave
faq.answer: Moisture drips continually from the cave’s ceiling, making the stone seem to weep. Plague has turned the runoff rancid, and it fosters virulent fungal growth.
The Husk is a rare corrupted elemental deep within Weeping Cave. Lingering alchemical blight in the surrounding earth and water has warped it.

angles.text: As a druid, you see nature turned against itself in Weeping Cave. The plague of undeath has corrupted its subterranean flora and elemental energies into violent monstrosities.
